subject: Renewal planning: commit uplift + price safeguard request
messages:
From: Alex Zhao <alex@novum.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning: committing + price hold ask

Hi Dylan / Monica,

Appreciate all the support this year — Novum's usage grew faster than we modeled and we're up for renewal in late May. A few asks from our side to kick off negotiation: 

- We want to increase committed units by ~35% for the next 12 months (predictable spend for our Q3/Q4 launches).
- Can Redwood offer a 3-month price hold on baseline per-token rates if we take the uplift?
- We'd like a modest bridge credit (one-time) to offset migration/QA costs from our engineering changes.

I've attached a short invoice summary so you can see our run-rate and the proposed uplift range. Finance is looped on procurement next steps (procure@novum.ai).

Two asks for you: a rough ballpark on economics if we take +35% commit, and a proposed MAP/MAP-like mutual action plan we can share internally.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of ML Ops, Novum AI
Attachments: 2028-04-05-Novum-current_invoice_summary.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alex Zhao <alex@novum.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-06T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: committing + price hold ask

Alex — thanks for the context and the summary. We can absolutely structure something that balances Novum's runway with Redwood's capacity planning. High-level thoughts (prelim):

- +35% committed units: we can offer a tiered discount schedule with a stepped effective rate break at +20% and +35%. Example attached (prelim-pricing-v1).
- 3-month price hold: we can include a short-term price hold on baseline rates as part of a 12-month commit amendment if the uplift is contracted and invoiced upfront or via a 3-month accelerated billing cadence.
- Bridge credit: we can provide a one-time $40k credit applied over the first two invoices post-renewal, or convert to additional tokens if you prefer.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll circulate a formal mutual action plan and the draft pricing worksheet.
2) Ben (CC) will validate margin/discount levers and confirm what we can lock vs. what requires leadership sign-off.
3) Monica will propose an onboarding cadence so we don't hit throughput cliffs during your Q3 launch.

Attaching the preliminary worksheet for ballpark math. Fine to iterate; want to present a single path to your procurement team.

Best,
Dylan
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Attachments: 2028-04-06-Novum-prelim-pricing-v1.pdf (PDF, 4 pages)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-07T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: committing + price hold ask

Quick internal — Dylan, Monica:

Reviewed the prelim numbers. A couple of constraints and options:

- We can support a 3-month price hold tied to a +30% committed uplift with a 12-month term and a 90-day acceleration clause. Anything beyond +50% needs finance escalation.
- Bridge credit: $40k is doable, or we can structure it as 10% extra committed tokens in month 1 and 2 (favors usage).
- Burst protection (for your Q3 launch): recommend adding a transient burst buffer (uncommitted capacity) with a capped overage rate to avoid throttles.

If you want to make the price hold unconditional we'd need an upfront deposit or a payment milestone. Otherwise we can do invoice-anchored protections. I'll draft the pricing bullets for legal and ops.

-Ben
Senior Account Executive
Attachments: (none)

From: Alex Zhao <alex@novum.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Finance Ops <procure@novum.ai>
Date: 2028-04-08T14:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: committing + price hold ask

Dylan / Ben — thanks, this is helpful. Procurement has two priorities before May sign-off:

1) A clear mutual action plan with milestones (SOW sign, billing milestone, onboarding dates).
2) A written confirmation of a 90-day price hold tied to +30% committed uplift. Procurement will accept an accelerated billing milestone rather than upfront deposit.

If Redwood can commit to the 90-day hold + $40k bridge credit (or token equivalent) and provide a MAP by EOD Monday 2028-04-10, we can push the renewal to a signed PO the week of 2028-04-17.

Also: can you provide a DocuSign-ready amendment (term + pricing) and a simple SOW outline for services onboarding? Our legal team prefers minimal redlines for amendments.

Appreciate it — Alex

Date: 2028-04-10T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: committing + price hold ask

Alex — thanks, we can meet the procurement asks and will get you a single package to review Monday. Confirmations below: 

- Price hold: 90 days from contract effective date tied to a +30% committed uplift over current baseline (12-month term).
- Bridge credit: $40,000 applied as account credit across the first two invoices post-effective date OR convertible to 12% extra committed tokens in month 1 and 2 (your choice).
- Burst protection: transient buffer of 20% additional capacity with capped overage pricing for the first 90 days to support your Q3 launch.
- Billing: accelerated billing milestone acceptable instead of deposit — recommended schedule included in attached MAP.

Next steps (action owners):
- Dylan: Deliver DocuSign-ready amendment + MAP (Mon 2028-04-10 EOD).
- Ben: Finalize pricing exhibit and margin sign-off.
- Monica: Draft onboarding SOW and services timeline.

I'll attach the Doc and spreadsheet now; please confirm which bridge credit option you prefer and we'll route to legal.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Attachments: Novum-MAP-2028-v1.xlsx (Excel, 1 sheet); 2028-04-10-Novum-amendment-docusign.pdf (PDF, DocuSign-ready)
